title: Three Divisors
summary: Given an integer n , return true if n has exactly three positive divisors.
statement: Given an integer n , return true if n has exactly three positive divisors. Otherwise, return false. An integer m is a divisor of n if there exists an integer k such that n = k × m .
constraints: Count positive divisors, including one and n itself.
Return true exactly when the total divisor count is three.
hints: A number has exactly three divisors precisely when it is the square of a prime.
Check that n is a perfect square, then test its integer square root for primality.
r=isqrt(n); require r*r==n and no divisor from 2 through isqrt(r).
Divisors normally pair. Exactly one unpaired middle divisor requires a square p^2, and having only 1,p,p^2 requires p to be prime.
editorial: Divisors normally pair. Exactly one unpaired middle divisor requires a square p^2, and having only 1,p,p^2 requires p to be prime.
